requests.discriminates: every generated identity in one comparison: a missing, renamed, recoded, recategorised, reflagged or retexted message changes the fingerprint, and the 16 chunk fingerprints localise the difference to about 138 identities
requests.subject: diagnostics.roster

requests.discriminates: the three per-message flags are carried independently: every flagged identity at this pin, plus two unflagged controls, so a port that drops a flag or applies it to the wrong message is caught by name
requests.subject: diagnostics.identity

requests.discriminates: the category ordinal is the wire contract, not the name: three CategoryError identities -- a plain one, one that is elided in the compatibility pyramid and one that reports unnecessary code -- against one CategoryMessage and one CategorySuggestion, so ordinal 1 is witnessed against three different flag sets. No generated identity is CategoryWarning at this pin (the 2,211 identities are 1,385 Error, 806 Message and 20 Suggestion), so ordinal 0 has no witness here
requests.subject: diagnostics.identity

requests.discriminates: the code range and the extra-message block: the lowest and highest codes and the first extraDiagnosticMessages entry, which a port that only reads diagnosticMessages.json would be missing
requests.subject: diagnostics.identity

requests.discriminates: message text is compared as raw bytes: escaped backslashes, escaped double quotes, a literal '{' with no closing brace, a brace pair that is not a placeholder, four placeholders and a repeated placeholder. The two sides are not the same API: Go's Message.String is the only exported accessor for the unexported text field and returns it verbatim ('return m.text', which the pin marks as debugging only), while tsr_diagnostics exposes those bytes as the public `text` field and has no Display or to_string, so the row carries one text field and a match witnesses the bytes and their reachability, not a Stringer port
requests.subject: diagnostics.identity

requests.discriminates: an unknown key resolves to nothing rather than to a neighbour: the empty key, the name without its code suffix, a case-folded key, leading and trailing space, a longer key with the same prefix, the ad-hoc key '-1' and an absent key, against one valid control
requests.subject: diagnostics.identity

requests.discriminates: Go's Key is a byte string, so a non-UTF-8 key is a legal query that resolves to nothing; a Rust lookup keyed on &str cannot express it at all
requests.subject: diagnostics.identity-bytes

requests.discriminates: Category.Name returns the lowercase reporting word for the four defined categories and panics for anything else; the panic is the contract, not a default string
requests.subject: diagnostics.category

requests.discriminates: the generated stringer is a different function from Name: it returns the Go constant identifier and renders an out-of-range value as Category(n) instead of panicking
requests.subject: diagnostics.category

requests.discriminates: with no arguments Format returns the text unchanged, placeholders and all: it short circuits on len(args) == 0 before the replacement pass, so '{0}' survives verbatim rather than becoming empty or an error
requests.subject: diagnostics.format

requests.discriminates: every occurrence of a placeholder is replaced, out-of-order indices select by number not by position, and arguments beyond the highest placeholder are ignored without error
requests.subject: diagnostics.format

requests.discriminates: a placeholder whose index is at or past len(args) panics with 'Invalid formatting placeholder'; the len(args) == 0 short circuit means the same text with no arguments at all does not panic
requests.subject: diagnostics.format

requests.discriminates: only {(\d+)} is a placeholder: empty, spaced, signed, hexadecimal and full-width-digit braces stay literal, a leading zero still parses as the same index, a doubled brace keeps its outer characters, and an index that does not fit an int panics rather than being ignored
requests.subject: diagnostics.format

requests.discriminates: Go repairs arguments with strings.ToValidUTF8(arg, U+FFFD) before substituting, which collapses a whole run of invalid bytes into one replacement character rather than one per byte; valid multi-byte text and an embedded NUL pass through untouched. The last three rows pin the limit of that observation rather than extending it: an argument no placeholder consumes never reaches the output, and core.SameMap copies rather than repairing the caller's slice in place, so Go's eager repair of every argument is invisible through Format and a port that repairs at substitution time is byte-identical on all thirteen rows
requests.subject: diagnostics.format

requests.discriminates: no generated message text contains a newline at this pin, so multiline diagnostic text can only arrive through an argument or an ad-hoc message: newlines, CRLF and tabs inside an argument are substituted verbatim, and a multiline text keeps its line breaks around the replacement
requests.subject: diagnostics.format

requests.discriminates: an absent locale is the zero Locale, which getLocalizedMessages rejects as language.Und before any matching happens; the explicit tag 'und' and the English tags must all land on the built-in English text, whose table entry is nil rather than a loaded map
requests.subject: diagnostics.localize

requests.discriminates: every one of the 13 shipped translation tables is actually reached and returns its own bytes for the same identity; English is the first matcher entry, not a missing one -- loc_generated.go declares language.English at index 0 and localeFuncs[0] is nil -- so an English tag matches and still falls back to the built-in text, and tr-TR is the 14th and last entry. The order is load-bearing: getLocalizedMessages indexes localeFuncs by the matcher's index, so a port that builds the table array in another order serves the wrong language
requests.subject: diagnostics.localize

requests.discriminates: translated text moves the placeholder and changes the quoting around it, so substitution has to run on the translated string, not on the English one
requests.subject: diagnostics.localize

requests.discriminates: which table a non-exact tag selects: a bare language, a sibling region, a script subtag, an unshipped region of a shipped language, an unrelated language, a private-use tag and the undefined tag. The table's size and fingerprint identify the choice, so a wrong fallback is visible even when one probe key happens to agree
requests.subject: diagnostics.table

requests.discriminates: the per-table manifest F1a owes F1b: for each of the 13 embedded tables, how many keys it holds, how many of them the generated switch still resolves, how many are stale, and a fingerprint of its whole sorted contents. A regenerated or re-ordered table changes the fingerprint; a table that failed to decompress collapses to size zero
requests.subject: diagnostics.table

requests.discriminates: the selected table is memoised in a process-global sync.Map keyed by tag: repeating a locale in one process must return the same bytes, and an interleaved different locale must not leak its table into the next lookup
requests.subject: diagnostics.table

requests.discriminates: Localize with a nil message resolves the key itself and panics with 'Unknown diagnostic message: ' plus the key when it does not resolve; the panic text carries the key, so an empty key and an absent key are distinguishable failures rather than one generic error
requests.subject: diagnostics.localize

requests.discriminates: Localize's nil-message branch resolves the key itself through keyToMessage and reaches the same identity as the by-pointer call under every locale, including a translated table and an argument. The operation is Localize, not keyToMessage: the lookup is the part Rust already has -- by_key, witnessed by the identity cases -- so recording this case against keyToMessage would file an implemented operation as missing
requests.subject: diagnostics.localize

requests.discriminates: the negative control for a missing translation: an identity the table does not carry falls back to the English text rather than to an empty string, and each row records whether the selected table actually held the key
requests.subject: diagnostics.localize

requests.discriminates: Message.Localize takes ...any and runs StringifyArgs first, so a non-string argument reaches Format as its %v rendering and an invalid-UTF-8 string is still repaired; this is the public path a caller actually uses
requests.subject: diagnostics.message-localize

requests.discriminates: StringifyArgs returns nil for an empty argument list rather than an empty slice, passes a string through untouched including invalid bytes, and renders everything else with %v -- so nil becomes '<nil>', negative zero keeps its sign and a slice gets Go's bracketed form
requests.subject: diagnostics.stringify

requests.discriminates: an ad-hoc message is a runtime-owned Message with code -1, category Error and the key '-1': its text is never a static identity, it is never translated whatever the locale, and it still goes through the same placeholder substitution and the same missing-argument panic
requests.subject: diagnostics.adhoc
